voice: ElevenLabs eleven_v4, Jack (BVPhWQykET1TSvfGzrUr), English, one take, split into lines, inner pauses capped at 0.22 s, no tempo change; take 1

lines.text: The village gave us one rule. Never go past the stone gate into the forest. At midnight, past the gate, someone started playing gamelan.
lines.beat_before: hook: the torch on the stone gate; past it, in the black between the trees, a pale arm held out in a dancer's pose

lines.text: My friend was already walking toward it. He wouldn't answer me. He was walking in time.
lines.beat_before: through the gate; my friend ahead on the path, walking in time to the gamelan, his head tilting

lines.text: Every time my torch came back to the trees, she was there. Dancing. Slowly. A little closer.
lines.beat_before: the torch swings off into the trees and back: she is there, dancing, nearer each time

lines.text: Her feet never touched the ground. And her arms kept reaching, further than arms should go.
lines.beat_before: her feet hang above the leaves; her arms reach, too long, toward the light

lines.text: I found him at the stream. His arm was black and swollen with bites. And something was moving under his sarong.
lines.beat_before: the music stops; the stream; my friend sitting in it, his back to me; the torch finds his arm (the gong)

lines.text: The elders never blamed her. They blamed us. We broke the rule. I still don't know if he came back.
lines.beat_before: the torch swings up from him: the dancer behind him, her arms round him; back to the gate
